message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Natural abundance | Protium ≈ 99.98 %, Deuterium ≈ 0.02 %, Tritium negligible |
| **Physical State (Room Temp)** | State | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (20.3 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| | Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Vapor pressure (at 25 °C) | 1.3 × 10⁻⁴ atm |
| **Chemical Properties** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Acidic strength | Very weak acid (H⁺ in solution) |
| | Basicity | Very weak base (H⁻ in hydrides) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Typical bond lengths | H–H ≈ 0.74 Å |
| | Typical bond angles | 180° (linear) in H₂ |
| | Polarity | Non‑polar covalent bond in H₂ |
| | Solubility in water | 0.0006 g g⁻¹ (≈ 0.6 g L⁻¹) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | High (e.g., in liquid ammonia, ether) |
| **Spectroscopic** | Rotational spectrum | Microwave region (≈ 2.1 cm⁻¹) |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Electronic transitions | UV–visible absorption at 121.6 nm (Lyman‑α) |
| **Isotopic Differences** | Deuterium | Mass ≈ 2.014 u, heavier, lower zero‑point energy, stronger bonds |
| | Tritium | Mass ≈ 3.016 u, radioactive (β⁻ decay, half‑life ≈ 12.32 yr) |
| | Isotopic substitution effects | Alters vibrational frequencies, reaction rates (kinetic isotope effect) |
| **Thermodynamic** | Standard enthalpy of formation (H₂(g)) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy (H₂(g)) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Applications & Roles** | Fuel cell fuel | Produces electricity + water (H₂ + ½O₂ → H₂O) |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid H₂ + liquid O₂ (high specific impulse) |
| | Hydrogen bonding | Strong in water, acids, bases |
| | Stellar fusion | Proton‑proton chain (H → He) powers stars |
| | Industrial processes | Ammonia synthesis (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (only water vapor) |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability range (air) | 4 % – 75 % (v/v) |
| | Explosion limit | 4 % (lower) – 75 % (upper) |
| | Storage pressure | 200–700 bar for compressed gas; cryogenic liquid at ~20 K |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic, but can cause hypoxia by displacing oxygen |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, with one proton and one electron.
- **Two stable isotopes**: Protium (most common) and deuterium; tritium is radioactive.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms covalent bonds readily; participates in acid–base chemistry as H⁺ or H⁻.
- **Energy‑dense fuel**: Combustion yields only water, making it attractive for clean energy technologies.
- **Key in astrophysics**: Fusion of hydrogen nuclei powers stars and drives nucleosynthesis.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
